claim: `CaRefCatalogCore` owns local namespace-lifecycle safety and does not authorize when a GC invocation may perform catalog CAS relative to another invocation's adopted seal; that cross-object ordering belongs to `CaRefPreFoldDrainCore`.
A catalog deletion from `Removing` to absent requires positive terminal cleanup evidence for the exact opaque life id in the authoritative adopted row.
A catalog deletion from `Removing` to absent is forbidden when the authoritative adopted life row carries a durable hold.
A catalog deletion must match the complete exact `Removing` row observed by the mutator, including the full-catalog token, so it cannot delete a replacement row.
Catalog deletion does not require physical emptiness: `_ckpt`, stream, `_snap`, and `_files` residue may remain for the perpetual janitor or a family-specific sweep.

Before any fold, `REBUILD`, or `DEFER` decision, the production GC actor must read the currently adopted parent seal, drain every eligible catalog row, conclusively resolve every exact CAS, and take a fresh catalog cut.
Fresh opaque life ids make residue from a dead life structurally inert; reusing a dead id can make a reborn life's first read reach predecessor bytes.
A `Live` catalog row is safe only when its life's `_ckpt` exists; this protects against both an over-broad janitor and a fenced or token-stale creator installing late.
Catalog reconciliation requires both a terminal creator fence and an exact catalog token; stale unconditional reconciliation can delete a `Live` successor.
No catalog record may survive an absent logical name, even when physical residue remains across repeated create/drop cycles.
`INV_RECONCILE_SAFE_BRIEF` is not a valid gate because its proposed state formula rejects the legitimate transient state where a creator fence is terminal before `_ckpt` creation.
`CatalogTargets` must be derived only from the exact `Live`/`Removing` catalog plan key set, and `BeginRound` must freeze exact `_ckpt.committed_through` as `roundCte`.
`WalkStep` may exact-read only keys through the inclusive `roundCte` bound.
If a required key at or below `roundCte` is missing, the fold must reassert a hold without consulting `maxSeen` or any `LIST` observation.
`ScanComplete` may succeed only after every catalog target reaches CTE or resolves as held.
A target held at the start of a fold round must follow the same resolution path even when `LIST` returns no information.
The ref-delta intake has no quiet or expected-next 404 frontier: every catalog target must resolve through its exact CTE.
`CteExact` requires `committedThrough[t] = MaxDurable(t)` for every table, and `RoundCteNoRegression` requires `roundCte[t] <= committedThrough[t]`.
`HoldReleaseRequiresFold` requires that no fold debt remains before a hold can be released.
Under the amended v9 intake, `LIST` is a zero-trust hint; fold progress advances arithmetically and destructive work requires a per-namespace frontier proof.

The retired `_sab_fix_ckptwitness` and `_witness_corruptgap` obligations are unconstructible because `_ckpt.committed_through`, rather than `_ckpt.checkpoint` or a higher `LIST` witness, is now the exact bound and every missing key at or below it creates a hold.
`CaRefLaneCore` models six ownership states: `Ready`, `Writing`, `Wedged`, `NeedsRecovery`, `Closed`, and `Faulted`.
A captured predecessor runtime remains owned by its handle while the non-authoritative logical-name slot may publish a distinct successor after removal/rebirth or same-life self-remount.

Write and resolver operations must capture runtime provenance: `StartWrite` stores `lane_runtime` in `attempt_runtime`, `BeginResolve` carries it into `resolver_runtime`, and observations record `observation_runtime`.
The reference lane validates per-runtime projections of `cache_id` and `durable_id` during write, install, observation, resolution, and recovery transitions.

Applying a successor observation through an old resolver handle violates `NoOldHandleRetarget`; the observation must be attributed to the runtime in the current slot, not to the stale resolver runtime.
The relink composition seam requires confirmation in `Ready`, promotion using the exact confirmed identity, and source deletion only with receiver ownership.
The relink seam depends only on the small `Ready` certification contract; the reference lane is modeled from semantic obligations rather than reconstructed from nested implementation decisions.
The `cas/ns/` janitor must capture the exact physical life id encoded in a returned `LIST` key and continue targeting that id when a delayed delete resumes after same-name rebirth.
The janitor must not re-resolve a logical name at delete time; exact physical identity captured at nomination is the safety boundary.
Fresh life-id allocation and physical-id capture are independent requirements: reusing an id or re-deriving the target from the logical name can delete a live successor's data.
A janitor nomination is valid only when it came from an actual listed physical id; `NominationCapturedPhysicalId` checks this provenance.
`CaRefNsCleanupStaleLeaderCore` deliberately excludes the adopted-parent/fresh-cut protocol, local catalog deletion evidence and holds, and synchronous physical cleanup from namespace removal.

Before `DEFER`, ordinary fold adoption, or `REBUILD` adoption, GC actor B must read the authoritative parent, resolve every eligible exact catalog CAS, complete the hot-stream `LIST`, take one fresh authoritative catalog cut, and build the ref-walk plan.
An old catalog request that returns after lease takeover is safe only if the successor actor consumed the token first or no successor invalidated the proof under which the old request lands.

The pre-fold plan carries opaque life ids separately from catalog lifecycle states and carries the fresh cut's complete catalog token/value into ref-plan intake without importing fold lifecycle from `CaRefDeltaIntakeCore`.
A ready parent cannot proceed to normal fold, `REBUILD`, `DEFER`, or a fresh-cut continuation while an eligible catalog deletion remains unresolved.
If an exact catalog row is still `Removing` after an ambiguous or conflicting storage result, the actor must refresh the full-catalog token and retry; only an absent row is conclusive completion.

A missing or undecodable authority cannot be replaced by a seal discovered through enumeration for catalog deletion; honest `REBUILD` restores authority and returns, leaving the drain to a later invocation.
The authoritative catalog cut used for ref-plan intake must be taken after the completed hot `LIST`; a cut taken before `LIST` can omit a current successor and classify it as dead debris.
A predecessor listed later but absent from the authoritative cut is counted once, excluded from the life-id plan, and must never be used as a `DEFER` reason.
A later cut containing `{successor_life, Removing}` must produce the singleton life-id plan `{successor_life}`, never the predecessor life id.
A stale predecessor proof must not delete a successor in `Removing`; exact deletion must match life id, lifecycle state, and the full-catalog token.

`IntakeConsumesFreshPostDrainCut` requires ref-plan intake to consume the exact token/value pair exported by `TakeFreshCut`, including life id and lifecycle state, and its plan projection must equal the walkable life-id set.
An exact delete or external catalog resolution that invalidates the full-catalog token requires a complete serial rescan before the next candidate or successor decision.
The all-row pre-fold drain may decide only when its remaining eligible-row set is empty; `CompletionDrained` defines `phase = "done" => remaining = {}`.
The exact `_ckpt.committed_through` frontier is the only durable authority for ref-log install, acknowledgement, successor allocation, snapshot publication, and seal publication.
Immutable object producer fences are separate from checkpoint-CAS admission fences; after a remount, the current writer may checkpoint exactly one valid old-fence successor at `frontier + 1`.
Every checkpoint CAS binds an exact sampled token, so an intervening checkpoint update invalidates it, while an already-issued request may still linearize after a fence move.
Recovery after an ambiguous response must perform an exact `_ckpt` read and validate both the sampled token and the exact chain before installing.
Seal publication consists of conditional creation of the immutable seal followed by a same-contribution checkpoint CAS that atomically advances `lastEpochSeal` and `committedThrough`.
Snapshot bodies must be published before checkpointing them, and neither snapshots nor seals may name a value above `_ckpt.committed_through`.
Ref-log ids are per-namespace contiguous ids derived from state, and an id whose create outcome is ambiguous must not be reused under the every-attempt rule.
An absent expected-next id is not a safe frontier in a sparse id space because recovery cannot distinguish a gap from the end and can install state missing every record above the gap.
Recovery closes the frontier by conditionally occupying the next slot with an in-band epoch seal; a late predecessor PUT is either adopted or fenced by that real object.
Every ref-log write is a create-if-absent operation; an unconditional PUT must not overwrite an epoch seal.
Recovery must treat paginated `LIST` as a zero-trust hint rather than truth and must walk the ref-log tail by arithmetic point reads.

GC may delete a ref log only when `_ckpt` covers it; deleting a durable id below an unchanged checkpoint token makes a 404 indistinguishable from the frontier and can cause recovery to seal over adopted data.
Snapshot cleanup may delete only snapshots strictly below the current `_ckpt` base; deleting the snapshot still named by `ckpt.base` must fail closed as corruption after exact-key revalidation.

A sealer must merge `_ckpt` by semantic maximum rather than write back a stale sampled body, because stale write-back can regress the base to 0 and make the next mount report an empty namespace over live data.
`ConfirmedRelinkNeverDangles` guarantees that a promoted receiver with answer `yes` and a durable receiver `+1` before confirmation references only live blobs.
The relink protocol must durably publish the receiver's `+1` before calling confirm; a confirm before that evidence exists does not protect the later promotion.
A confirm `yes` requires exact `ManifestRef` equality between the sender's committed row and the durable binding at confirmation time.
A confirm must require sender-lane quiescence for the whole tenure, including absence of pending work and an active leader.
A poisoned sender apply must cause confirm to return `unknown`, even if the tenure has closed and the lane appears quiescent.
A sender instance that loses the mount fence or current-writer authority must cause confirm to return `unknown`.

A single incomplete GC `LIST` page can permanently skip a durable receiver `+1`: the namespace cursor advances past the omitted transaction, the sender `-1` folds, and a deduplicated blob reaches physical deletion while a promoted manifest still references it.
The relink theorem is conditional on complete `LIST` discovery in the shipped pre-v9 GC; the confirm protocol itself cannot repair a journal-discovery hole.

The v9 regression pair treats enumeration as a zero-trust hint, advances fold work by `cursor + 1`, and requires per-namespace frontier proof for destructive work; `CaRefTableSnapshotLogCore_sab_scanistruth` remains red while `CaRefDeltaIntakeCore_v9_hintomission` is green.
The historical `_sab_holeylist` red is retained as a pre-v9 shipped-GC defect witness and must not be interpreted as a v9 implementation failure.
In-degree is a set-presence merge keyed by `(blob, source_id)` and applied in strict transaction-id order; a `del` whose key is absent is a silent no-op.
`GFold` and `GSettle` are separate steps, so a `+1` durable after a round's fold cut is invisible to that round's settlement.
Gate 0 is only an availability filter and authorizes nothing; safety belongs to gate 1, so modeling gate 0 would create a false impression of two independent safety sources.

A namespace inactive while global writer epochs advance must close every skipped epoch in order with an empty sequence-1 `EpochSeal` before its later consumer can authorize recovery, fold, or destruction.
A direct numeric epoch transition `E -> E + 2` cannot authorize recovery, fold, or destruction because the missing `E + 1` seal violates `INV_NO_EPOCH_SKIP`.
A decoded terminal seal in an epoch cannot authorize recovery past the same-epoch frontier.
The recovered owner set must use an `EpochSeal` as its checkpoint base rather than treating an arbitrary checkpoint as the owner-set base.
CAS correctness claims require an executable counterexample when a rule is removed; a green check that cannot go red is not evidence.
CAS operations must fail closed under ambiguity: an operation that may have landed must not be treated as one that did not.
Generic MergeTree, Replicated, and Keeper code must not learn CAS concepts; every accepted exception to that minimal upstream footprint must retain its reasoning.
A fallback is acceptable only when uncertainty concerns the mechanism; uncertainty about the source must abort and retry rather than silently taking another route to the same peer.
The pre-release pool format does not owe compatibility scaffolding or a dual protocol; a format bump is preferred because no persisted production data exists.
Suspected protocol-step costs must be instrumented before optimization decisions are made.
No path may lose acknowledged data or delete an object still named by a committed reference; any current gap must be named, mechanized, executable as a test, and fixed before release.

`stale_edge` denotes a blob whose every source edge names a manifest that no longer exists; its positive in-degree is pinned forever, so incremental GC cannot reclaim it and only `ca-gc-rebuild` can clear it.
The S42 reproduction showed `stale_edge` values of 12 before restart and 67 after restart, while the run had zero environmental failures and 12,998 acknowledged blocks.
Stale-edge residue remained permanently nominated-free across 145 GC rounds: the key-set fingerprint did not change and both `pending_gc` and `awaiting_gc` stayed zero.
The authoritative residual check is the in-degree run; counting `adds > removes` is only a heuristic because in-degree is a last-wins presence set.

The epoch-1 stale-edge root cause is a race in which a precommit `+1` folds, an allocation fault aborts the build, an orphan-manifest sweep deletes the now-unowned manifest without first decrementing its edges, and the folded `+1` remains permanently unreclaimable.
The dead-precommit skip was not the S42 cause because `dead_precommits_skipped` was zero on both nodes; the skipped `-1` path never fired.

The epoch-1 cohort was confirmed six-for-six as orphan-sweep deletions of manifests carrying unmatched `+1` edges; the two epoch-4 attributions remain unreliable and must not be presented as eight-for-eight.

The orphan-sweep fix direction is unresolved between emitting `-1` edges before deleting a manifest and refusing to sweep manifests whose edges may already have folded; neither should be implemented without the cost model.
The in-degree reducer must not be changed to fix stale edges; the defect is upstream in the orphan-sweep premise.

CAS is a `metadata_type = content_addressed` disk back-end for `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree` that stores each part file once by content hash, allowing replicas to share an object-storage pool without byte duplication or zero-copy replication.
The CAS pool layout includes `blobs/`, `cas/refs/`, `cas/manifests/`, `roots/`, and `gc/`, with a hot/cold split and incarnation tokens in the object model.
The writer protocol uses mount startup with `server_root_id` owner claim, durable-monotone `writer_epoch` and `build_sequence`, and the build → precommit → upload → promote sequence.

The GC protocol includes leader election and lease, fold → retire → fence → recheck → trim/reclaim rounds, orphan removal through source-edge in-degree, exact-token deletes, shard incarnation, attempt-scoped generations, and snap pruning.
CAS introspection is exposed through `clickhouse-disks ca-fsck`, `ca-gc-dryrun`, `system.content_addressed_log`, and `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log`.
Release readiness still requires capability gate B31, real-S3 GC validation, a backup/restore runbook, `SYSTEM` control commands B197, RustFS integration tests B125, and repository hygiene B131.
The D1 shard-incarnation and registry-removal work deleted `gc/registry`, stamps `ShardIncarnation` in `CasRootShardCodec.h`, and discovers the universe with `LIST`-based `discoverUniverse`.
TLA+ conventions require `_sab_*` and `_bug` sabotage configurations to produce counterexamples, while a `violation` from `_witness_*` means the negated reachability state is reachable.

The model suite uses the pinned official `tla2tools` jar revision `30cc360` with SHA-256 `cc4803dce2a8ffaf0f5920a9dc39df4b5ee34ab4cb53fb58ac557277a7e516b3`; the former TLC 2.19 revision `5a47802` is rejected.
A suite runner must assert each expected outcome by the name of the invariant or property it must break; a runner that checks no property is not evidence.

The audited `cas-gc-rebuild` branch had no model/code safety risk: whenever a model diverged from the shipped mechanism, the code preserved the same safety conclusion through an equal-or-stronger mechanism.

The canonical GC core requires exact-token deletion, atomic cascade with deletion, registry fencing from the committed namespace universe, and fresh observation of stale dependency evidence before publication.
A GC round that held back an unreadable shard must make no destructive decision, and the clamp-suppression guard prevents physical deletion while an unfolded delta could still touch the blob.
Two-phase graduation publishes `delete_pending` with a round CAS before physical delete, preventing a deposed leader's stale pass from deleting a live blob.

A durable never-reused per-shard incarnation plus a newborn shard fenced to the current GC round replaces the namespace registry's safety role, but reclaim still waits for the shard journal to be fully folded.
A due GC graduation must force a fold before physical deletion, while a non-destructive round may re-adopt the sealed in-degree snapshot; deferral is bounded.
Graduation to `delete_pending` requires confirmed durable `Condemned` evidence from a write-completion callback or synchronous meta re-read; otherwise the entry carries to the next round.

A durable precommit edge must make an adopter's build root structurally reachable before adoption, and commit must re-check the whole closure and fail closed on absence; each half is independently necessary.
A precommit that records its blob closure lazily from a tree object can record an empty closure after the tree disappears, causing a blob to leak forever.

With durable precommit closure before adopt/observe and same-pass GC recheck, promote-time revalidation of already-tokened leaves is redundant; dedup adoption, tokenless-leaf presence HEAD, condemned checks, and operation order remain load-bearing.

Ref tables are persisted as an immutable snapshot plus an append-only log of strictly increasing transaction ids, and recovery uses ordered point reads while cleanup deletes only durably observed objects.

The v9 ref-table protocol derives contiguous ids from state, frees an id only under the every-attempt rule, reads the `_ckpt` base, walks arithmetically, and closes the frontier by occupying the next slot with an epoch seal.

The pool-wide ref-delta fold makes every catalog `Live`/`Removing` life a mandatory target, snapshots exact `_ckpt.committed_through`, walks arithmetically to that bound, and treats every missing required key as a durable hold independent of `LIST`.

`CaRefCatalogCore` keeps the catalog bounded under churn by using fresh opaque life ids and authorizes removal only with matching terminal evidence, no hold, and deletion of the complete exact `Removing` row.

A pre-fold GC invocation must resolve all eligible exact catalog CAS operations, complete hot `LIST`, take one fresh cut, and build the sole ref plan before fold, `REBUILD`, or `DEFER`; ambiguous results cannot be treated as completion.
The pre-fold plan is keyed only by opaque life id, and stale full-catalog token/value, stale cut ordering, absent-listed classification, and identity-blind deletion are each independently unsafe.
The perpetual namespace janitor captures a physical life id from a `LIST` page and delayed deletion never derives its target from a reborn logical name.

The writer cleanup lifecycle precommits ownership, atomically replaces the precommit with the committed owner on promote under the current epoch, and cleans failed builds in resolve-grant → remove → retire order.
An unresolved every-attempt grant remains an in-memory duty while the mount lives and cannot be retired.

The v9 mount recovery layer captures `(actor, generation, op)` identity at admission and rechecks generation after I/O before every publication; an `Occupied` `slot-occupy` result must be resolved by comparing bytes.
A recovery result returning after self-remount is refused, and a dead lane's conditional create cannot be admitted under a successor generation.

`Occupied` with an `EpochSeal` terminates a concurrent recovery walk, while an operation acknowledged after a lost write is forbidden unless byte comparison proves that operation's bytes were durably written.

The FORGET-only disk lifecycle is one-way: terminal states imply a latched fence, GC is destroyed and unrestartable, a started FORGET completes under fairness, and the GC scheduler eventually stops ticking after `Vanished`.

The historical `CaB140DangleMerge` fix requires journal trimming only up to the cursor inside the committed snapshot and atomic commitment of that cursor with the edges; either half alone can lose data.
The original epoch-based reclamation GC with a global epoch and per-writer pins was superseded by the incarnation-token design because no epoch machinery exists in the shipped code.
Per-incarnation body keys were rejected because they reintroduce incarnation into keys and manifests, require a 404-then-`LIST` read path, and break pure-content manifests.
A meta-absence-means-clean tombstone variant was rejected because clearing a condemned marker in place is unsafe under the add-only freshness-meta proof and no such code landed.
The per-candidate minimum-active-build watermark mechanism was replaced by precommit-first reachability; the surviving requirement is that build sequence numbers come from a monotone counter.
